title: the DSG equipment costs and weights

banner.title: The DSG NEW EQUIPMENT COSTS AND WEIGHTS, R525: printed pp. 56-57 (pdf 57-58) - the chapter frame (the equipment primarily for underground exploration but usable in any AD&D campaign, listed with average cost and typical encumbrance, descriptions to follow, the specific uses tied to the climbing, mining and underground water travel rules) and the Table 35 cost/weight grid: the twenty general rows (air bladder 15 gp and 20 gp, basket large 5 sp and 80 gp, basket small 2 sp and 40 gp, beacon 40 gp and 200 gp, birdcage 5 sp and 50 gp, box small gold 100 gp and 20 gp, box small lead 20 gp and 20 gp, crampons 40 gp and 50 gp, crowbar 3 gp and 75 gp, drill iron 5 gp and 50 gp, grappling hook 75 gp and 75 gp, lantern waterproof 50 gp and 50 gp, lard pint 5 cp and 20 gp, oil waterproofing 1 gp and 20 gp, pickaxe 20 gp and 200 gp, powder chalk 2 sp and 20 gp, pulley 25 gp and 60 gp, reed hollow 1 sp and 1 pc, shovel 10 gp and 180 gp, whistle 1 sp and 1 pc) and the four transportation rows (boat collapsible 500 gp and 600 gp, canoe small 100 gp and 800 gp, canoe large 300 gp and 1,600 gp, kayak 250 gp and 500 gp); and the equipment for proficiencies: the fourteen initial costs and minimum spaces (animal trainer 100 gp and 1-20 acres, armorer 1,250 gp and 20 x 20, blacksmith 1,000 gp and 30 x 30, boatwright 1,000 gp and 50 x 120, bowyer/fletcher 250 gp and 20 x 20, carpenter 400 gp and varies by task, gem cutter 2,225 gp and 15 x 15, leatherworker 300 gp and 15 x 15, miner 750 gp and varies, potter 600 gp and 20 x 30, smelter 2,000 gp and 50 x 50, stonemason 250 gp and varies, weaponsmith 1,500 gp and 40 x 30, weaver 500 gp and 30 x 30), the rule that a proficiency is only partially effective without the necessary space, and the raw-materials exclusion - the costs do not include the raw materials (an armorer or blacksmith needs iron, hardwood or coal), which run 11-20% (1d10 + 10) of the finished work value
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~7205-7265) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 131 = the printed p. 56 window, idx 133 = the p. 57 window); the compiled-tables appendix has an equipment reprint but it shares the same failed OCR layer. AN OCR-FAILURE ROUND, THE THIRD OF THE MINING STRETCH: the Table 35 grid failed in both machine reads with genuine conflicts between them - the djvu garbled every sp as the Cyrillic ар and dropped the basket-small cost entirely, while the Capture layer dropped the lard, reed and whistle cells and mislabeled others - and the vision passes over Curtiss's screenshots wobbled the currency units (air bladder 15 sp/5 sp/15 gp across passes). The grid was settled by Curtiss reading the physical printed p. 56: air bladder 15 gp (the direct read that also exposed the sp-pattern assumption as unsafe), basket small 2 sp and 40 gp, basket large 5 sp and 80 gp, crowbar 3 gp, pulley 25 gp and 60 gp, reed 1 sp and 1 pc, whistle 1 sp and 1 pc. The machine reads corroborate the clean cells (the beacon, boxes, crampons, drill, grappling hook, lantern, oil, pickaxe, powder and shovel rows agree across djvu and Capture), the four transportation rows, and the full fourteen-row proficiency list (both reads agree on every cost; the areas share only the trivial degree-sign glyph garble). The reed and whistle weight prints 1 pc - the book's own abbreviation in the coin-weight column, pinned as printed per the never-repair rule. The new-equipment descriptions and the transportation prose (children 138-139) land NEXT round per the content-density rule; the descriptions text is already extracted and clean in both machine reads. The R518 water-travel, R520 mining and climbing seams are noted; nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: Two tables pin: Table 35 as a 24x2 grid (cost in copper pieces normalized, weight in gold-piece coin weight - the twenty general rows plus the four transportation rows), and the proficiency equipment as a 14x2 grid (initial cost in gold pieces, minimum space in square feet with the sentinel -99 for the animal-trainer acres and the carpenter/miner/stonemason Varies rows). The raw-material percent pins as dice + sides + add consts (1d10 + 10 giving the 11-20% range) per the R508 convention. The frame rules pin as prose bools: the any-campaign usability, the cost-and-encumbrance listing, the space-required rule, the raw-materials exclusion with the armorer/blacksmith example, and the printed 1-pc pin. The physical-read provenance is load-bearing for the seven OCR-failed cells (the air bladder, basket-small, basket-large, crowbar, pulley, reed and whistle cells); the R517/R521/R522 lessons apply. The climbing/mining/water-travel seams are noted; nothing auto-credits.

prev_record: - R524 LANDED 2026-10-17: commit 7c7074c (census 447 -> 448,
pushed 0573b9b..7c7074c), THE DSG HIRELING LOYALTY AND THE
P. 55 HAZARDS, printed pp. 54-55 (pdf 55-56) - the hireling
loyalty: a PC group cannot usually run a mine alone (even
with a miner-proficiency supervisor, a large mine needs
hired strong arms; adventurers better as scouts and guards
when the claim is questionable or monsters possible),
loyalty insignificant in iron or copper mines but a
precious-metal or gemstone find a great temptation, the
standard DMG page-36 Loyalty Check with the foreman as the
liege, the + or - 10% security modifiers (a post-shift
search +10%, no PCs present at shift end -10%), pay
evaluated against the mine's value (the 1,000 gp of
diamonds for a 20 gp wage), and the failed check not an
immediate grab-and-run - the DM weighs the NPC's
Intelligence, only perhaps 8-or-less attempting unplanned
theft, exceptionally high Intelligence preparing the theft
and the getaway or concealment, the thief stealing
1d6 x 10% of his daily output; the natural hazards:
flooding from a tapped underground water body or digging
below the water table (adjudicated from the DM's map, the
below-level escape very difficult, at-level a race to the
exit, above-level easy; the flooded mine needing draining
or pumping), and mine cave-ins (shoring partially
preventing but never eliminating - shored every 10 feet 2%
weekly, no shoring 50%, partial interpolated; the
earthquake 1d4 x 10%, heavy rain or flood 1d3 x 10%,
burrowers like umber hulks and ankhegs 1% per hit die; the
d100 location roll designating one end 01 and the other
100, e.g. a 30 on a 1200-ft shaft about 360 ft from the
entrance; the automatic 20-foot-long 10-foot-thick fallen
ceiling; chain reactions checked normally); and the
unnatural hazards: the unnamed evil lurking deep in the
earth at DM creativity (the burial-ground undead, the
concerned deep-dwelling monsters), the drow and duergar
regarding mineral wealth as their own with intervention
rising in direct proportion to the mine's value, and the
planar-gate risk - some horrid lower-plane denizen finding
a path into the world up a deep-plunging tunnel. A
CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every
number. THE MINING BLOCK IS NOW FULLY CLOSED (all
children flipped), and the natural/unnatural hazards were
the last open children of the big underground-environment
chapter (pp. 36-55) - the chapter parent line is closeable
at the next census check. SEAMS: DMG p. 36 loyalty, R520
shoring (the 10-ft intervals match), R511 chain
reactions, R518 water travel. Pinned as rules/dsgmine6.h
(prefix dnsw, verified free; 38 inlines - 18 consts, 20
bools, no tables - a pure prose round). Spec 24,783
bytes, md5 1f37314d48a5eb0cbb1ca2024922da41 (user-side
identical - no ./bn rewrite). Engine applied 7 then 0/7.

consts.name: dntaT35RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 35 cost/weight grid carries twenty general rows plus the four Transportation rows (the collapsible boat, the two canoes and the kayak).

consts.name: dntaProfRowCount
consts.comment: the proficiency equipment grid carries fourteen proficiencies from animal trainer through weaver.

consts.name: dntaRawMatDice
consts.comment: the raw-material cost roll is one die.

consts.name: dntaRawMatSides
consts.comment: the cost of raw materials is 11-20% of the finished work value - 1d10 + 10.

consts.name: dntaRawMatAddPct
consts.comment: the +10 add makes the 1d10 raw-material roll the 11-20% range.

bools.name: dntaUsableAnyCampaign
bools.comment: the new equipment, while primarily intended for underground exploration, can be used in any AD&D game campaign.

bools.name: dntaListedWithCostAndEncumbrance
bools.comment: the new equipment is listed with its average cost and typical encumbrance, with descriptions following the lists.

bools.name: dntaUsesTiedToRules
bools.comment: specific uses of some equipment are explained under the rules for climbing, mining, and underground water travel (the cross-chapter seams).

bools.name: dntaProfSpaceRequired
bools.comment: the proficiency equipment gives the initial cost and the minimum space the operation requires - if the necessary space is not available, the proficiency is only partially effective.

bools.name: dntaProfCostsExcludeRawMaterials
bools.comment: the given costs do not include the raw materials characters must buy before using most proficiencies - an armorer or blacksmith needs iron, hardwood or coal for the forge; the raw materials cost 11-20% (1d10 + 10) of the finished work value.

bools.name: dntaReedWhistleWeightPrintedPc
bools.comment: the reed and whistle weight cells print as 1 pc (the book's own abbreviation in the coin-weight column, pinned as printed per the never-repair rule).

bools.name: dntaAnimalTrainerSpaceVaries
bools.comment: the animal trainer needs little specialized equipment - at most a few harnesses or leashes - but the training of most animals requires a great deal of room, generally some kind of outdoor space, with shelter and food if boarding animals (the 1-20 acres area varies).

bools.name: dntaCarpenterMinerStonemasonVary
bools.comment: the carpenter area varies by task, and the miner and stonemason areas vary - the three Varies rows of the proficiency grid.
